{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mi-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"518e8bf4b14afba1e83d9d78cf1f4bf9ae5197e7699eefdaec3398466a326006","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mi-class-std:lineage:37","source_registry_sha256":"7af7437894a2c63b20529c8a1ed7c10696796036051dd6666178ab579008ca37","source_liveness_sha256":"e81e5179580dc89fb25fdf5194e9f75291db3aa019fc21ccfe32c38d1a9df42f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Railroad crossings and parking","heading":"C — Railroad crossings and parking","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Railroad crossings and parking

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
A stop sign at a railroad crossing means you must stop even when no train is visible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Unless signs say otherwise, school buses, for-hire passenger vehicles, gasoline trucks and other vehicles hauling hazardous materials must stop and confirm no train is coming even without a stop sign or signal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
Passive crossings have no flashing lights or gates; they rely on advance warning signs, pavement markings and crossbucks with yield or stop signs at or just before the tracks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
At a passive crossing, slow or stop as needed, yield to trains, check both directions, make sure every track is clear, and never race a train. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
Active crossings warn of a train with some mix of gates, flashing lights, message signs, and bells or other sounds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
Stop whenever crossing bells ring, lights flash, or the gate is down or moving, and never drive through, around or under an activated crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
After a train passes, wait until the gates rise, lights and bells stop, and you are sure all tracks are clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A01
Never stop on tracks, always expect a train, look both ways, and avoid changing gears while crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A01
On a snowy road, cross tracks with enough speed that you will not get stuck. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A01
When traffic may be backed up near a crossing, do not start across unless your vehicle can clear the far side of the tracks by at least 6 feet. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A01
Once crossing lights and gates activate or you hear a train horn, you have about 20 seconds before the train arrives. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A01
If you are stuck on the tracks and the gates are activated or a train is clearly coming, get everyone out and far from the tracks right away, then call 911. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A01
If stuck with no activated lights or gates and no train in sight, get everyone out and away, then call the railroad's number on the blue Emergency Notification Sign and report the crossing ID. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A02
The crossing ID on the Emergency Notification Sign has six digits and one letter; railroad officials may slow, stop or divert a train, and you then call 911. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A02
An Emergency Notification System sign at or near a grade crossing gives a phone number and the crossing's US DOT number for reporting emergencies or broken warning devices. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A02
Whenever you park, turn off the engine, set the parking brake rather than trusting the transmission, take the keys and lock the vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A02
Before opening your door, watch for passing bicycles, motorcycles, mopeds and vehicles and check your mirrors. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A02
Opening the driver's door with your right hand turns you to look over your left shoulder for oncoming cyclists and pedestrians. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A02
Walk back to the driver's side facing oncoming traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A02
Parking downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb; parking uphill, turn them away from the curb; with no curb, turn them so the vehicle will not roll into traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A02
Always set the parking brake on a hill, because the transmission is not built to act as a brake. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A02
To parallel park, choose a space on the passenger side, signal, check mirrors, and pull alongside the car ahead of the space leaving 2 to 5 feet between you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A02
Brake, shift to reverse, check traffic behind, then back slowly while checking mirrors and looking over your right shoulder. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A02
Turn the wheel right as you start backing to angle the rear in, then turn the other way once the rear is mostly in, making an S turn that straightens the car. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A02
Center the car in the space, park no more than 6 to 12 inches from the curb, and check traffic before opening your door. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A03
Disabilities are not always visible, so someone without a cane or wheelchair may still be entitled to a disability space. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A03
Free parking is given only to vehicles showing a disability placard with a yellow free-parking sticker, which has stricter rules than a disability plate or placard. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A03
To use a disability space, you or your passenger must have a qualifying disability, such as blindness or a temporary or permanent condition that greatly limits walking or needs an assistive device, plus a disability plate or placard. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A03
Do not use a disability space if no occupant is disabled or the disabled person is not going into the store with you. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A03
Van-accessible spaces are wider to fit a wheelchair lift and ramp, so never park on their blue-striped area or block ramps and curb cuts. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A03
Local parking ordinances may be stricter than state law, with signs posted at city limits. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A03
The owner of an illegally parked vehicle pays the ticket, or the person leasing it if the vehicle is leased. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A03
Never park where no stopping, no standing or no parking signs are posted, or within 500 feet of a fire or crash. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A03
Never park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A03
Keep 20 feet from a fire station driveway on your side of the street, and 75 feet from it on the opposite side when marked. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A03
Never park within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F37 | anchor: A03
Do not park in front of a driveway, alley, theater, emergency exit or fire escape, or where you block the view of drivers turning at an intersection. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F38 | anchor: A03
Never park more than 12 inches from the curb or facing against traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F39 | anchor: A03
Keep at least 30 feet away from a stop sign, traffic light or flashing beacon when parking, and the same applies to a warning sign. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F40 | anchor: A03
Do not park on or under a bridge unless posted, on an overpass or in a tunnel, and outside city or village limits do not park in a highway lane when there is a shoulder. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F41 | anchor: A04
Do not park on a sidewalk, in front of a public or private driveway, or inside an intersection, crosswalk or marked bike lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F42 | anchor: A04
Stay 20 feet from a marked crosswalk, or 15 feet from an intersection that has no crosswalk. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F43 | anchor: A04
Double parking beside a legally parked vehicle, blocking a rural mailbox, and parking at a transit stop are all illegal. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0053]
